head: 8d8b212
target: Repos opt into the gate with a tracked marker file instead of local git config pointing at a repo-carried hooks dir.
incidental: the self-test moved to the repo's top-level scripts dir and out of the skill's tool list
usage text for the new install and sync commands
skill page lines describing the new install and sync behavior
agent-mode notes on spawning the examiners, reworded

questions.prompt: Before, opting in meant local git config pointing at a hooks dir the repo carried. Why does a tracked marker file replace that?

options.label: Reading the old hooks dir on every push made pushes too slow.
Git refuses to run hooks from a directory stored inside the repository.
The old setting held in one clone; fresh clones pushed ungated until set up again.
The tracked file also gates commits and merges, which the old hooks never did.

key_points: The old opt-in was local config, so only the clone that set it had the gate.
Nothing tracked said the repo was gated, so fresh clones could silently lack the gate.
The marker file is committed, so every clone carries the opt-in with the code.
The repo tree no longer carries a hooks dir for the gate.

questions.prompt: The pre-push hook must call the gate tool, but the plugin's install dir moves with every update. Where does the hook look for the tool, and who keeps that working?

options.label: The hook calls the tool at its path inside the plugin's install dir.
The hook calls a copy in the user's bin dir; sync refreshes it there.
The hook reads the tool's location from the repo's config on each push.
The hook fetches the tool from the project's public page when missing.

key_points: The plugin's install dir changes on every update, so a baked-in path would break.
The hook finds the tool on PATH, then at its fixed spot in the user's bin dir.
Sync copies the tool there and replaces the copy when it goes stale.

questions.prompt: A repo opted in long ago. Which of these are true today?

options.label: A clone whose pre-push hook was deleted pushes unchecked until sync runs again.
If the user already has their own pre-push hook, sync overwrites it.
If the marker was never committed, fresh clones get no gate.
If the gate tool is missing, the hook lets the push through.

key_points: The hook is local state; the marker brings it back only when sync runs.
Sync never overwrites a foreign hook; it says what line to add to it.
Without the marker committed, the opt-in stays in the clone that created it.
A missing gate tool blocks the push; the gate fails closed, never open.

questions.prompt: A teammate clones the repo on a new machine. They push before any agent session has run there. What happens to that push, and what gates their pushes after the first session?
key_points: The first push is not checked: the fresh clone has no pre-push hook yet.
The marker came with the clone, because it is tracked and committed.
The first session runs sync, which copies the gate tool to the user's bin dir and installs the hook.
After that, every push is blocked until a quiz passes.
